subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: Element symbol
hotspots.description: The letter at the center of each tile is the element's symbol. The dots around it are its valence electrons.
hotspots.positionHint: The flat tile with the element letter at the center of each diagram.
hotspots.function: Marks the element symbol at the center of the dot diagram.

hotspots.label: Valence electron dots
hotspots.description: The dots around each symbol are the valence electrons — sodium has 1, carbon has 4, chlorine has 7. One dot per valence electron.
hotspots.positionHint: The small dots arranged around the symbol on each tile.
hotspots.function: Shows the valence electrons as dots around the symbol.

hotspots.label: Dots that become bonds
hotspots.description: Carbon's four dots reach out to four hydrogen atoms. Each shared pair of dots becomes a covalent bond — together they build a methane molecule.
hotspots.positionHint: The assembled methane molecule below, visible when the bond-forming layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows shared dot pairs building a molecule.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. Three flat tiles float in a row, each carrying an element symbol with dots, lit with soft neutral studio light — no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive anywhere. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Tiles are soft off-white with a hairline edge; dots are small teal spheres; symbol letters are subtle raised or app-rendered glyphs (not mesh text). Strong saturated color is reserved for the small flat hotspot dots (coral / molecular-green / amber accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Tiles: soft off-white matte, roughness ~0.6, thin hairline edge. Dots: small muted teal spheres, roughness ~0.45. Symbol letters: app-rendered (no mesh text). No emissive channels anywhere — any glow is handled by app runtime UI.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: Lewis dot diagrams of three elements, built to be read as 'dots = valence electrons = a bonding map.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: three flat rounded tiles in a row (spacing ~1.2), each with a soft off-white face and hairline edge: (a) sodium — ONE teal dot above the center; (b) carbon — FOUR teal dots, one on each side; (c) chlorine — SEVEN dots (arranged one per side then paired as the rule requires, leaving one unpaired). The element letters (Na, C, Cl) are app-rendered at the tile centers (no mesh text).

2) BOND FORMING (toggleable layer): below the tiles, a methane (CH₄) ball-stick molecule assembles — the central carbon's four dots reach out to four hydrogen atoms (soft off-white, r~0.18) and each shared pair becomes a thin graphite rod (app animates dot → rod). The result is a standard CH₄ tetrahedral ball-stick.

3) DOT PLACEMENT (toggleable layer): a translucent placement overlay appears over carbon's tile — four faint corner brackets showing the rule 'one dot per side first, then pair'.

Camera: framed so the three tiles fill the upper area with the methane assembly below; auto-rotate default. Budget 5-9k triangles. Named nodes: Tile_Na, Tile_C, Tile_Cl, DotNa_01, DotC_04, DotCl_07, MethaneMolecule, Methane_Carbon, Methane_Hydrogens_04, Methane_Bonds_04, PlacementOverlay. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer.
